newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-HUMILITY THE KEY TO AUXERRE SUCCESS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HUMILITY THE KEY TO AUXERRE SUCCESS.

text.p: Auxerre coach Guy Roux, a firm believer in humility, said his team's shock European champions' league win over Ajax on Wednesday may have been prompted by his low profile approach to the game.
"This victory is a lesson for the French press. Usually we're all cocky before matches and then we cry. This time, it went the other way round," he told French television.
"That's why I'm now telling you there are still 90 minutes left before we're qualified for the quarter-finals."
Goals by Bernard Diomede and Steve Marlet gave the French champions a 2-1 success. Now, a draw at home to Rangers on December 4 would be enough for Auxerre to qualify.
"I'm sure the Scots won't take it easy. It is not the way they are and I'm happy we're not going to have to stage a friendly against them," he said.
Roux, who has been with Auxerre for almost 40 years and has been portrayed in comics as a stingy, down-to-earth peasant, had called on God to help Auxerre win in Amsterdam.
"Actually I had called on gods to helps us because we have Christians and Moslems at Auxerre. The gods have heard me. But there also were fine human beings on the pitch," he said.
Roux also paid tribute to Ajax, saying they were, like Auxerre, without a number of key players.
"We both had to do with what we had left in store. What we had left was not bad," he said.
Nigerian defender Taribo West said the team from Burgundy never had and doubts about the outcome. "We had faith in ourselves and we proved it. You know, we're a very strong team," he said.
West will miss the Rangers match because of two bookings.
